name: program_correlator
summary: Asof time-window join of two streams: ~/.cc/phantom_dom_events.jsonl (intent — what the user *tried* to do, captured by a Phantom-wrapper / browser-console miner) and ~/.cc/program_events/**/*.jsonl (truth — what actually landed on chain, captured by program_monitor). For each DOM event, finds chain events within a ±window (default 5s), then emits one correlation row carrying the closest chain event, the frequency distribution of programs and actions in the window, and the dimension_pack rgba. These rows are the training feed for the bot-vs-human / chain-intent classifier (GMM + XGBoost).
engine_pattern: Stream sort + bisect for O((D+C) log C) lookup. Stdlib only (bisect, collections.Counter). Polars-free; would benefit from polars.join_asof when D becomes large but not needed at current scale. When phantom_dom_events.jsonl is empty (miner not running yet), an optional --synth N flag synthesizes DOM rows from chain (back-dated 50-4500 ms) so the row format and aggregator can be validated end-to-end.
feeds_into: core/lib/pump_feature_extractor (correlation rows are a richer feature input than raw chain events alone)
core/lib/telegram (Tom has a bot pre-wired; high-signal correlations become telegram alerts)
ethics_and_authorization: DOM event ingest assumes the user OPTED IN via a consent flow (e.g., freetier_callback's terms+policies acceptance + friends_consent claim).
Chain side is public state; correlator never sees private keys or signed payloads.
Synthetic DOM rows are flagged payload.synthetic=true and source_url='phantom://synth' — clearly distinguishable from real intent in audits.

inbound_callers: future: pump_feature_extractor as enriched input source
